title: Constant-overhead simulation of finite tape programs
preamble:
import Definitions.Def_ExpandingCodes_PolynomialStretch_BinaryRuntime

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped Classical
open NKtLB
formal_statement:
theorem ExpandingCodes.Computation.TapeCompiler.compile_halts {R B L : ℕ} (P : ExpandingCodes.Computation.TapeProgram R B L) (O : Set (List Bool)) (inp : Inputs)
    (t : ℕ) (hh : P.halted (P.run inp t)) :
    (ExpandingCodes.Computation.TapeCompiler.compile P).HaltsWith O inp (1+2*t) (bitsSym (P.run inp t).output) := by sorry
natural_statement: Every finite source tape program has a canonical NKtLB machine simulation. A source execution halting after t instructions is simulated with the same output within 1 + 2t machine steps, for arbitrary oracle and input.
source: Algorithmic supporting lemma for Section 2 of Isaac M Hair and Amit Sahai, Expanding Codes with Polynomial Stretch; the explicit tape-machine implementation is formalized in ExpandingCodes.Computation.TapeCompiler.
proof_route: The proof establishes each instruction simulation, inducts over source executions, and transfers halting and output to the compiled machine.
solution_header:
theorem solution {R B L : ℕ} (P : ExpandingCodes.Computation.TapeProgram R B L) (O : Set (List Bool)) (inp : Inputs)
    (t : ℕ) (hh : P.halted (P.run inp t)) :
    (ExpandingCodes.Computation.TapeCompiler.compile P).HaltsWith O inp (1+2*t) (bitsSym (P.run inp t).output)
solution_body:
by
  exact @ExpandingCodes.Computation.TapeCompiler.compile_halts R B L P O inp t hh
